title: EmPower (aircraft power adapter)
wikitext:
{{Short description|Power connector used on passenger airplanes}}
'''EmPower''' is a brand name that refers to three different power outlets available on commercial airlines:
* 15-volt, 75-watt DC connector (now called '''EmPower Classic''' by the vendor)
* 5-volt, 10-watt USB power-only jacks<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.astronics.com/product?productgroup=Aircraft%20Electrical%20Power%20Systems&subproduct=in-seat%20power%2Fempower%C2%AE|title=Astronics In-Seat Power/EmPower|access-date=2017-10-06}}</ref>
* 110-volt AC power jacks (some also have an EmPower USB jack)

== Original 15-volt EmPower connector ==
15-volt [[Direct current|DC]] connector type found on many commercial [[airlines]] designed to provide power to travelers' electronic devices.  The system is limited to 75 watts.<ref>EmPower Product Description [http://www.astronics.com/products/cabin-power/other-products.asp] www.astronics.com Accessed 2011-01-16. {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150312164159/http://www.astronics.com/products/cabin-power/other-products.asp|date=2015-03-12}}</ref> The use of a special connector is to prevent laptops charging at altitude and ensure that only approved adapters can be used.

[[Image:empower jack.png|thumb|right|EmPower plug]]

Some airlines offer it only in business class or only in certain types of aircraft or flights.  Travelers in the 2000s bought EmPower adapters, frequently from [[duty-free shop]]s at airports, to run laptops and other electronic equipment without using battery power.

Supporting airlines include:
* Some [[Air France]] planes
* Some [[Air India]] planes
* Some [[American Airlines]] planes
* Some [[British Airways]] planes
* Some [[Qantas]] planes
* Some [[United Airlines]] planes
* Some [[Virgin Atlantic]] planes
* Almost all [[Alitalia]] planes
* Almost all [[Cathay Pacific]] planes{{Citation needed|date=November 2020}}

(The [[SeatGuru]] web site contains more detailed information on which flights support EmPower.)

Adapters exist to connect EmPower plugs to [[cigarette lighter receptacle]]s and most EmPower power adapters come with these.

EmPower is a [[trademark]] registered initially by Primex Technologies (VA) and assigned to Astronics Advanced Electronic Systems, Inc., in [[Kirkland, Washington]], United States.  Subsequently, the trademark has been expanded to include not just the [[Vendor lock-in|proprietary]] 15{{nbsp}}V DC connector but also the 120{{nbsp}}V 60{{nbsp}}Hz AC in-seat power (and video entertainment) systems.
[[American Airlines]] uses EmPower 120{{nbsp}}V AC outlets (standard 2 prong plus ground) on their newer 737s.

Many laptops will not function properly at 75{{nbsp}}W.
The new<ref name="astronicsaes_com-in-seat-power-supply">{{cite web|title=Astronics AES EMPOWER In-Seat Power|url=http://www.astronics.com/products/cabin-power/in-seat-power.asp}} 111101 astronicsaes.com</ref> {{When|date=November 2011}} 60{{nbsp}}Hz [[Alternating current|AC]] EmPower system provides more power than the [[Direct current|DC]] system.<ref name="astronicsaes_com-in-seat-power">{{cite web|title=Astronics AES EMPOWER Classic-DC In-Seat Power|url=http://www.astronics.com/products/cabin-power/other-products.asp}} 111101 astronicsaes.com</ref>

The AC EmPower system converts aircraft 400{{nbsp}}Hz AC or wild frequency power to standard 60{{nbsp}}Hz AC to prevent additional stresses in laptop chargers already stressed by reduced cooling at altitude. Laptops on this system will still charge batteries. Modern laptop batteries, however, include a temperature sensor that should compensate for the reduced cooling at altitude. This new system accepts various national power plugs and most laptop chargers will function properly at 120{{nbsp}}V 60{{nbsp}}Hz AC even if sold in 230{{nbsp}}V 50{{nbsp}}Hz AC markets.

[[Apple, Inc|Apple]] offered an EmPower [[MagSafe (Mac)|MagSafe]] power adapter for their [[MacBook]], [[MacBook Pro]], and [[MacBook Air]] lines of notebooks, and also included a cigarette lighter socket adapter.  However, this system would only run the computer without charging the computer's battery, and Apple warned users to never plug this device into a car's cigarette lighter outlet.<ref name="apple-magsafe">{{cite web|title=MagSafe Airline Adapter|url=https://manuals.info.apple.com/MANUALS/0/MA396/en_US/Magsafe_Airline_Adapter.pdf}} Accessed 2015-11-10.</ref>
This product was later discontinued. 

Even though EmPower adapters are rated at 15 volts instead of 12 volts like [[cigar lighter receptacle]]s, most accessories made for the so-called "12-volt outlets" have enough voltage tolerance to allow for a voltage as high as 15 without step down DC-to-DC converter.

== Modern AC and USB EmPower outlets ==
[[Image:Universal_Airline_In-Seat_Power_Socket_110V_AC.svg|thumb|right|Universal airline AC socket layout]]

EmPower is a 120-volt universal connector type found on many commercial [[airlines]] designed to provide power to travelers' electronic devices. The system is limited to 200{{nbsp}}VA. The EmPower universal AC outlet is compatible with [[AC power plugs and sockets|power plugs]] from over 170 countries and is designed such that 110{{nbsp}}V AC power is not present at the outlet until a suitable plug is fully inserted.

The AC EmPower system converts aircraft 400{{nbsp}}Hz AC or wild frequency power to standard 60{{nbsp}}Hz AC.
